scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, India sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. MA Agarwal anchored the innings with a resolute 9, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Australia's bowling response was spearheaded by Josh Hazlewood (5/8), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. India's total of 36/10 (21.2 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Australia embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 90 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 51 from JA Burns, complemented by a commanding 70-run stand between Matthew Wade and JA Burns that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.39 RPO. R Ashwin (2/16) maintained tight lines for India, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 93/2 (20.6 ov), Australia successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

summaryTab.matchStory: India posted 244 in the opening innings with Virat Kohli (74) providing key resistance. R Ashwin's 5-wicket haul dismantled Australia for 191, handing the advantage to India. India posted 36 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships. Australia held their nerve in the fourth-innings chase, reaching the target to seal a famous victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Adelaide Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 244/10 (93.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Australia countered with 191/10 (72.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 29 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, R Ashwin delivered a masterclass for India (15 Runs & 7 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 54%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, India faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by Pat Cummins (8 Wickets), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 8 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While India produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
